# Rationalism Has Risen Against Schiller and Dewey

Messrs.[^1] Schiller's and Dewey's theories have suffered a hailstorm of contempt and ridicule.[^2] All rationalism has risen against them.[^3] A hailstorm of contempt and ridicule[^4] throws so much sidelight upon that rationalistic temper to which I, William James,[^5] have opposed the temper of pragmatism.[^6]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Messrs."
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Schiller's and Dewey's theories have suffered a hailstorm of contempt and ridicule."
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "All rationalism has risen against them."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "a hailstorm of contempt and ridicule"
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means]] "William James"
[^6]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "throws so much sidelight upon that rationalistic temper to which I have opposed the temper of pragmatism."

# Pragmatism Is Uncomfortable Away From Facts

Pragmatism is uncomfortable away from facts.[^1] Rationalism is comfortable only in the presence of abstractions.[^2]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Pragmatism is uncomfortable away from facts."
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Rationalism is comfortable only in the presence of abstractions."
=== FILE: Objective Truth Must Be Something Non-Utilitarian.md ===
---
aliases: []
tags: []
---

# Objective Truth Must Be Something Non-Utilitarian

This pragmatist talk about truths in the plural, about their utility and satisfactoriness, about the success with which they 'work,' etc., suggests to the typical intellectualist mind a sort of coarse lame second-rate makeshift article of truth.[^1] Such truths are not real truth.[^2] Such tests are merely subjective.[^3] As against this, objective truth must be something non-utilitarian, haughty, refined, remote, august, exalted.[^4] It must be an absolute correspondence of our thoughts with an equally absolute reality.[^5] It must be what we OUGHT to think, unconditionally.[^6] The conditioned ways in which we DO think are so much irrelevance and matter for psychology.[^7] Down with psychology, up with logic, in all this question![^8]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "This pragmatist talk about truths in the plural, about their utility and satisfactoriness, about the success with which they 'work,' etc., suggests to the typical intellectualist mind a sort of coarse lame second-rate makeshift article of truth."
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Such truths are not real truth."
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Such tests are merely subjective."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "As against this, objective truth must be something non-utilitarian, haughty, refined, remote, august, exalted."
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "It must be an absolute correspondence of our thoughts with an equally absolute reality."
[^6]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "It must be what we OUGHT to think, unconditionally."
[^7]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "The conditioned ways in which we DO think are so much irrelevance and matter for psychology."
[^8]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Down with psychology, up with logic, in all this question!"
=== FILE: Truth Becomes a Class-Name for Working-Values.md ===

# Truth Becomes a Class-Name for Working-Values

The pragmatist clings to facts and concreteness, observes truth at its work in particular cases, and generalizes.[^1] Truth, for him, becomes a class-name for all sorts of definite working-values in experience.[^2] For the rationalist it remains a pure abstraction, to the bare name of which we must defer.[^3]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "The pragmatist clings to facts and concreteness, observes truth at its work in particular cases, and generalizes."
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Truth, for him, becomes a class-name for all sorts of definite working-values in experience."
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "For the rationalist it remains a pure abstraction, to the bare name of which we must defer."
=== FILE: The Rationalist Accuses Us of Denying Truth.md ===

# The Rationalist Accuses Us of Denying Truth

When the pragmatist undertakes to show in detail just WHY we must defer, the rationalist is unable to recognize the concretes from which his own abstraction is taken.[^1] He accuses us,[^2] Messrs.[^3] Dewey, Schiller and their allies,[^4] of DENYING truth; whereas we have only sought to trace exactly why people follow it and always ought to follow it.[^5]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "When the pragmatist undertakes to show in detail just WHY we must defer, the rationalist is unable to recognize the concretes from which his own abstraction is taken."
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "He accuses us"
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Messrs."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as a Theory of Truth]] "Dewey, Schiller and their allies"
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "of DENYING truth; whereas we have only sought to trace exactly why people follow it and always ought to follow it."
=== FILE: The Ultra-Abstractionist Prefers the Pale and Spectral.md ===

# The Ultra-Abstractionist Prefers the Pale and Spectral

Your typical ultra-abstractionist fairly shudders at concreteness: other things equal, he positively prefers the pale and spectral.[^1]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Your typical ultra-abstractionist fairly shudders at concreteness: other things equal, he positively prefers the pale and spectral."
=== FILE: A Rich and Active Commerce Between Thoughts and Experiences.md ===
---
aliases: []
tags: []
---

# A Rich and Active Commerce Between Thoughts and Experiences

Pragmatism[^1] only follows[^2] the example of the sister-sciences, interpreting the unobserved by the observed.[^3] It brings old and new harmoniously together.[^4] It converts the absolutely empty notion of a static relation of 'correspondence'[^5] between our minds and reality, into that of a rich and active commerce (that anyone may follow in detail and understand) between particular thoughts of ours, and the great universe of other experiences in which they play their parts and have their uses.[^6]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Pragmatism"
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "only follows"
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "the example of the sister-sciences, interpreting the unobserved by the observed."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "It brings old and new harmoniously together."
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "It converts the absolutely empty notion of a static relation of 'correspondence'"
[^6]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "between our minds and reality, into that of a rich and active commerce (that anyone may follow in detail and understand) between particular thoughts of ours, and the great universe of other experiences in which they play their parts and have their uses."
